1. The *Karmavācanā* for Abandoning the Boundary (*sīmā-utsarga-karman*): - Twenty-four *jñapti-karmas*. - Forty-seven *jñapti-dvitīya-karmas*. - Thirty *jñapti-caturtha-karmas*. Although the causes for performing a *karman* are not strictly limited to one hundred and one, they do not exceed this number when categorized by type. Regarding the method of *karman*, it must be executed with complete precision to constitute a valid *karman*;
here, only the general outline of the procedures is presented. [The section on] the *Karmavācanā* for Abandoning the Boundary.
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
The Saṃgha has previously established an internal boundary (*antar-sīma*) so that there may be a single recitation of the Prātimokṣa for one residence.

If the time is right for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha, out of its forbearance, grant permission for the Saṃgha to relinquish the original boundary within the single recitation of the Prātimokṣa for one residence."
Thus it was announced:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen! The Saṃgha has previously established an internal boundary so that there may be a single dwelling place for a single recitation of the Prātimokṣa."
Now, within this single recitation of the *Poṣadha* at this single monastic residence, we relinquish our original boundary (*prakṛtasthiti*).
Which elders consent to relinquishing the original boundary within this single recitation of the *Poṣadha* at this single monastic residence? Those who consent remain silent;
those who do not consent should speak.

“Since the Saṃgha has completed the relinquishing of the original boundary within a single recitation of the Prātimokṣa at this one residence, and because the Saṃgha remains silent in approval, this matter is thus upheld.
2. The Karmavācanā for Establishing the Internal Boundary: These four locations constitute the internal boundary; therefore, they are not excluded.
To prevent the internal fault of losing one's robes, it is therefore subsequently prescribed that within the robe, one should exclude [the boundary] by saying: "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This bhikṣu so-and-so declares the characteristics of the four boundaries; this characteristic marks the interior boundary, and that characteristic marks the exterior boundary."
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha permits, let the Saṃgha establish an internal boundary because the Saṃgha shall perform the recitation of the Prātimokṣa at a single residence.
This is the formal motion (*jñapti*). "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!"
This bhikṣu named [Name] has described the boundary marks of the four directions: this mark is the inner boundary and that mark is the outer boundary.
Because the Saṃgha dwells in a single location and performs the *poṣadha* together, it establishes the inner boundary.
"Whichever elders consent to establishing an internal boundary for the purpose of a single recitation of the *Poṣadha* at one residence, let those elders remain silent;
whoever does not consent, let them speak.

"The Sangha has finished establishing the internal boundary for the purpose of a single recitation of the *Poṣadha* at one residence. Since the Sangha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld."

3. The Ritual for Delimiting the External Boundary (Bāhirā-sīmā). Regarding the method for delimiting the boundary: one should first mark out the characteristics of the internal boundary (*antarā-sīmā*). Within those internal boundary marks, one then marks out the characteristics of the external boundary. One first binds the external boundary and subsequently binds the internal boundary. The reason the external boundary is situated within [the internal] is that there may be certain residences where an external boundary is not required. "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!..."
This bhikṣu named [Name] has described the boundary marks of the four directions; the Saṃgha has established an internal boundary.
Within this, the Saṃgha has established such an area as an external boundary for the site of receiving the precepts.
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, let the Saṃgha designate this much ground as a boundary for the place of receiving the precepts.
This is the formal motion (*jñapti*). "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!"
This bhikṣu named [Name] has described the boundaries of the four directions; the Saṃgha establishes an internal boundary.
Within this, an area of such extent is established by the Saṃgha as an external boundary for the place of receiving the precepts.
"Whichever elders approve of delimiting this much ground within these inner boundaries to constitute the outer boundary for the site of receiving the precepts, let those elders remain silent;
whoever does not approve, let them speak."

“The Sangha has completed the formal act of demarcating this much ground within the inner boundary as the outer boundary for the site of receiving the precepts. Since the Sangha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.”
4. The Formal Act for Binding the Non-Forfeiture of Robes (Akaṭhina-kamma) “Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
At this single residence, the inner boundary is established for the recitation of the Prātimokṣa.”

Within this context, excluding villages and their boundaries, and excluding forest hermitages and dwellings, for all remaining single residences, one may perform the *poṣadha* ceremony once and establish the practice of not losing one's robes.
"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha permits, let the Saṃgha, at a single residence, recite the Prātimokṣa together and establish the *anāpatti* (non-offense) rule regarding robes.
This is the formal motion (*jñapti*). "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!"
Within a single dwelling where the *poṣadha* is recited and an internal boundary (*antarā-sīmā*) has been established—

excluding villages and their precincts, as well as forest hermitages (*āraṇya*) and houses— the remaining area constitutes a single dwelling for the recitation of the *poṣadha*, wherein the practice of not losing one's robes (*acīvara-nāśa-dharma*) is maintained.
Which elders approve that this single residence shall perform a single *poṣadha* ceremony and establish the rule for not losing one's robes? Since you are silent, those who approve;
those who do not approve should speak.

“The Saṃgha has heard this: the procedure for the ‘not losing one’s robe’ (*akālacīvara*) has been completed by means of a single recitation of the Prātimokṣa at this single residence. Since the Saṃgha remains silent in approval, this matter shall be held thus.”

“May the Sangha listen, O Venerable Ones! There are fourteen persons within the Sangha who perform the formal act (*karmavācanā*): one capable of performing the legal act, one capable of distributing the bedding of the Sangha, one capable of spreading the bedding of the Sangha, one capable of distributing the cakes of the Sangha, one capable of assigning and inviting [guests], one capable of managing the novices, one capable of distributing the rice-gruel of the Sangha, one capable of managing the gardeners, one capable of distributing the robes of the Sangha, one capable of distributing the rain-cloths of the Sangha, the master who distributes the medicine, the one who oversees the property of the Sangha day and night, the one who oversees the coarse goods of the Sangha, and the one who constantly guards the dwelling place.”
"Venerable sirs, this bhikṣu so-and-so is capable of acting as the *śuddhika-dharma-karaka* for the Saṃgha.
If it is the proper time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to grant its consent, let the Saṃgha appoint this bhikṣu so-and-so as the *śuddhika-dharma-karaka* for the Saṃgha."
Thus he makes the motion:
"Venerable Sangha, listen!
This bhikṣu, so-and-so, is capable of performing the duties of a *saṃgha-śuddhika-dharma*."
"Venerable sirs, monk so-and-so is acting as the *saṃgha-śuddhikara*.
Whichever elders approve of monk so-and-so acting as the *saṃgha-śuddhikara*, let them remain silent;
whichever do not approve, let those elders speak."
“Monks, the monk [Name] has completed his duties as a *saṃgha-śuddhikara*. Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.
“Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
"Venerable sirs, this bhikṣu so-and-so is capable of acting as the distributor of bedding for the Saṃgha.
If the time is right and the Saṃgha is willing to grant its consent, let the Saṃgha appoint this bhikṣu so-and-so as the distributor of bedding for the Saṃgha."
Thus he makes the formal announcement: "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
The bhikṣu named So-and-so is capable of acting as the distributor of bedding and furniture for the Saṃgha."
"Whichever elders approve of this monk so-and-so acting as the distributor of bedding for the Sangha, let them remain silent;
whichever do not approve, let those elders speak.
"The Sangha has completed its appointment of the monk so-and-so as the distributor of bedding for the Sangha. Since the Sangha remains silent in approval, this matter is thus upheld."

"Fourteen cases are summarized into two persons; the rest of the legal procedures may be understood accordingly. **The Procedure for the Confession of Saṃghāvaśeṣa Offenses.** The Buddha was staying in Śrāvastī.
The Elder Kāḷudāyī intentionally emitted semen and incurred a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense, which he concealed for one day.
This Elder said to the bhikṣus: "Venerable sirs!..."
"I have intentionally emitted semen and committed the offense of *saṃghāvaśeṣa*, and I have concealed one instance of that offense. What should I do?
The bhikṣus did not know what to do and reported this matter to the Buddha.
The Buddha addressed the bhikṣus:

"You and the bhikṣu Kālodāyin have committed the offense of intentional emission of semen, for which you have incurred a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense. Because one of you concealed this offense, you must undergo parivāsa for as long as it was concealed, performing the various duties with a humble mind."
"Furthermore, if there are bhikṣus who have committed such offenses, they too should be granted parivāsa. The bhikṣus said,
"Venerable Sir!"
"How should he act?
The Buddha said:

"In the midst of the assembled Sangha, this bhikṣu Kālodāyin should bare his right shoulder, remove his leather sandals, enter the assembly, prostrate at the feet of the bhikṣus, kneel with his right knee on the ground, join his palms, and say:”
"Venerable sirs, please attend to me with one mind!
I, the bhikṣu Kālodāyin, intentionally emitted semen and thereby committed a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense; I have concealed this single offense."
In order to purify this offense, I request the *parivāsa* penance from the Saṃgha for as many days as I concealed it.
Venerable Saṃgha!
I, the bhikṣu Kālodāyin, intentionally emitted semen and committed a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense; one such offense was concealed.
"In order to remove this offense, I shall grant you the *parivāsa* for as many days as it was concealed,
out of compassion.
Having spoken thus a second and a third time, he concluded.

"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This bhikṣu Kālodāyin committed the offense of *saṃghāvaśeṣa* by intentionally emitting semen; he concealed one such offense.
To expiate this offense, he shall beg for *parivāsa* from the Saṃgha for as many days as it was concealed.
He said: "Venerable Saṃgha!
I, the bhikṣu Kālodāyin, intentionally emitted semen and committed a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense; I have concealed one offense."
“In order to purify this offense, just as one is granted *parivāsa* for the number of days it was concealed, out of compassion.
If the Saṃgha’s time has come, may the Saṃgha listen with patience: the bhikṣu Kāliya committed a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense by intentionally emitting semen; he concealed one offense.
"In order to remove this offense, just as [penance] is given for the number of days it was concealed, so shall *pārivāsika* be granted.
Thus I announce. "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!"
This bhikṣu Kālodāyin intentionally emitted semen and committed the offense of *saṃghāvaśeṣa*, which he concealed for one day.
To expiate this offense, the Saṃgha shall now grant him *parivāsa* according to the number of days it was concealed.

What should I do now? The bhikṣus did not know what to do.
They reported this matter to the Buddha.
The Buddha said to the bhikṣus:

"You and the bhikṣu Kālodāyin have committed the saṃghāvaśeṣa offense of intentional emission of semen. Because one of you did not conceal the offense, you shall undergo six nights of *mānatva*, followed by six nights of ascetic practice (*karkaśa*) and humble service for the sake of the Saṃgha."
Furthermore, there is a bhikṣu who has committed such an offense that he should be granted the six-night *mānatva*. The bhikṣus said:
"Venerable One!"
"How should he grant it?
The Buddha said:

"In the midst of the assembled Sangha, the bhikṣu Kālodāyin should bare his right shoulder, remove his leather sandals, enter the assembly, prostrate himself at the feet of the bhikṣus, kneel with his right knee on the ground, join his palms, and say: [as follows]"
"Venerable sirs, please attend to me with one mind!
I, the bhikṣu Kālodāyin, intentionally emitted semen and committed a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense; this single offense was not concealed."

Venerable Saṃgha!
I, the bhikṣu Kālodāyin, intentionally emitted semen and committed a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense; this single offense was not concealed.

"Venerable Saṃgha, please listen!..."
This bhikṣu Kālodāyin committed the saṃghāvaśeṣa offense of intentional emission of semen; he did not conceal this single offense.
To expiate this offense, he requests the six-night *mānatva* from the Saṃgha.
He said: "Venerable Sangha!
I, the bhikṣu Kālodāyin, intentionally emitted semen and committed the offense of saṃghāvaśeṣa; I have not concealed this single offense."
"In order to remove this offense, out of compassion, we grant him six nights of *mānatta* penance.

If the Saṃgha is ready and the Saṃgha grants its consent, let the Saṃgha hear: Bhikṣu Kāliya has intentionally emitted semen and committed a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense; he has not concealed this single offense.

"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!"
This bhikṣu Kālodāyin intentionally emitted semen and committed a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense; he did not conceal this single offense.

"Whichever elders here consent that the bhikṣu Kālodāyin, having intentionally emitted semen, has committed a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense—one offense not concealed—and that for the sake of purifying this offense, the Saṃgha now grants him six nights of *mānatva*, let those elders remain silent;

In this manner, it should be stated for the second time and for the third time:
"The Saṃgha has granted the monk Kālodāyin the *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense of intentional emission of semen; he did not conceal this single offense, and having completed the six-night *mānatva* penance."
"Because the Saṃgha has remained silent, this matter is thus upheld.

Within the assembly of the one-minded Saṃgha, the bhikṣu Kālodāyin should bare his right shoulder, remove his leather sandals, enter the midst of the Saṃgha, prostrate at the feet of the bhikṣus with his head to the ground, kneel on his right knee with palms joined, and say:
"Venerable elders, please attend to me with one mind!
I, the bhikṣu Kālodāyin, previously intentionally emitted semen and committed a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense; one offense was not concealed.

I requested from the Saṃgha six nights of mānatva, and the Saṃgha granted me six nights of mānatva. Having completed the practice, and for the sake of purifying this offense, I now request absolution from the Saṃgha.
"Venerable Saṃgha!
This bhikṣu Kāḷudāyin previously intentionally emitted semen and incurred a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense. Since he has not concealed this one offense, I grant him absolution from that offense."
“Out of compassion.
Thus it should be said a second and a third time.
11. The Karmavācanā for the Expiation of the Mānāpya. “In this matter, one bhikṣu should announce in the midst of the Saṃgha:”
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This bhikṣu Kāḷudāyin previously intentionally emitted semen and committed a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense; he has not concealed this one offense."

He said: "Venerable Saṃgha!
I, the bhikṣu Kālodāyin, previously intentionally emitted semen and committed a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense; I have not concealed this one offense."
He requested from the Saṃgha the six-night *mānatva* penance; the Saṃgha granted him the six-night *mānatva*, and he completed its observance.

"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to grant its ear, since the bhikṣu Kāḷudāyin previously committed the offense of saṃghāvaśeṣa by intentionally emitting semen, and as he has not concealed this one offense, the Saṃgha shall grant him absolution from this offense."
Thus he makes the motion: "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This bhikṣu Kālodāyin previously intentionally emitted semen and committed a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense; one offense was not concealed."

He requested the six-night *mānatva* from the Saṃgha; the Saṃgha granted him the six-night *mānatva*, and he has completed its observance. Now, for the sake of removing this offense, the Saṃgha grants him absolution (*abbhāna*) within the assembly.

"Whichever elders approve that the bhikṣu Kālodāyin, having previously emitted semen intentionally and thereby committed a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense, shall now—since he has not concealed this single offense—be granted absolution from the offense within this Saṃgha: let those elders who approve remain silent;
whoever does not approve, let them speak."
In this manner, he spoke a second and third time:

"The Saṃgha has granted the rehabilitation from the saṃghāvaśeṣa offense incurred by the bhikṣu Kālodāyin due to his previous emission of semen; one offense was not concealed, and the rehabilitation from that offense is now complete."
"Because the Saṃgha remained silent, this matter is thus upheld.
This Venerable Kālodayin, while still in the midst of performing the *mānatva* penance for six nights, committed another *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense by emitting semen; he did not conceal this offense.
He addressed the bhikṣus: "Venerable sirs!
Previously, I intentionally emitted semen and committed a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense; I have not concealed this single offense."
I requested from the Saṃgha six nights of *mānatva* penance, and the Saṃgha granted me six nights of *mānatva*.
While I was still performing the six nights of *mānatva* within the Saṃgha and had not yet completed it, I again committed a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense by emitting semen; this offense was not concealed.
"What should I do now?
The bhikṣus did not know what to do and reported this matter to the Buddha.
The Buddha said to the bhikṣus:
"You should deal with the bhikṣu Kālodāyin according to the original rule.
Should any other bhikṣu incur such an offense, he too should be dealt with according to the original rule."
The bhikṣus said: "Venerable One, how should it be given?"
The Buddha said:

"When the Saṃgha has assembled with one mind, the bhikṣu Kālodāyin should bare his right shoulder, remove his leather sandals, enter the midst of the Saṃgha, prostrate himself at the feet of the bhikṣus, kneel with his right knee on the ground, join his palms, and say:
'Venerable elders, please attend to me with one mind!'"
I, the bhikṣu Kālodāyin, previously intentionally emitted semen and committed a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense; one offense was not concealed.
I requested a six-night mānāpya from the Saṃgha, and the Saṃgha granted me a six-night mānāpya.
Having already practiced for several days, before those days were completed, I further committed a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense, one offense which I did not conceal.
In order to expiate this offense, I beg the Saṃgha for treatment according to the original rule.
"O Saṃgha!
This bhikṣu Kālodāyin intentionally emitted semen and committed a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense; he has further committed another offense, which he has not concealed.
For the sake of removing these offenses, I request that you grant him the original disciplinary treatment out of compassion."
"In this manner, it is said a second and third time.
12. *Mūlāpatti Karma*. Within this, one bhikṣu should announce in the midst of the Saṃgha:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!"
This bhikṣu Kālodāyin had previously emitted semen intentionally, thereby committing a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense; he did not conceal this single offense.
He requested from the Saṃgha a six-night mānāpya, and the Saṃgha granted him a six-night mānāpya.

This bhikṣu Kāḷodāyin was performing the *mānatva* penance for six nights within the Saṃgha; after he had already practiced it for several days, with several days yet remaining, he committed another *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense, which he did not conceal.
In order to remove this offense, he requests from the Saṃgha that he be treated according to the original rule. He says:
"O Saṃgha!..."
I, the bhikṣu Kālodāyin, intentionally emitted semen and incurred the saṃghāvaśeṣa offense; I have committed another offense as well, which I have not concealed.
Out of compassion, grant me the same disciplinary treatment as for the original offense.

"If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to grant its ear, the monk Kāḷudāyin, having intentionally emitted semen and thereby committed a *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense, has further committed another offense which he has not concealed."
"In order to remove this offense, he shall be treated according to his original case.
Thus it is announced.

The *jñapti-caturtha-karman* (the formal act consisting of one motion and three proclamations) is as follows: "The Saṃgha has granted the monk Kālodāyin the *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense for intentionally emitting semen. He has committed another offense of the same nature, which he did not conceal. The treatment according to his original case is now concluded."
“Since the Saṃgha has remained silent, this matter is thus upheld.

This bhikṣu Kāḷudāyin committed another offense while already under penalty; after he had completed the six-night *mānatva* penance within the Saṃgha according to his original disciplinary treatment, he said to the bhikṣus:
“What should I do now?”
The bhikṣus did not know what to do,
so they reported this matter to the Buddha.
The Buddha said:
"Perform the *āpattivyutthāpana-karman* (the ritual for emerging from an offense) for you all.
This bhikṣu Kālodāyin committed an offense while already under an offense; he has now completed the six-night *mānatva* penance within the Saṃgha according to the original disciplinary procedure."
"Furthermore, there are bhikṣus who have committed such offenses; they too should be granted the *karmavācanā* for the removal of offense.
The bhikṣus said, "Venerable One!"
"What is the procedure for the *karmavācanā* of absolution from the offense?
The Buddha said:

"In a one-minded assembly of the Saṃgha, the bhikṣu Kālodāyin should bare his right shoulder, remove his leather sandals, enter the midst of the Saṃgha, prostrate with his head at the feet of the bhikṣus, kneel on his right knee with palms joined, and say: "
"Venerable sirs, please attend to me with one mind!
I, the bhikṣu Kālodāyin, intentionally emitted semen and committed a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense; this single offense was not concealed."
I previously requested a six-night *mānatta* penance from the Saṃgha, and the Saṃgha granted me a six-night *mānatta*.

"O Saṃgha!

This bhikṣu Kālodāyin committed a further offense while already under penalty for a previous offense. Having completed the six-night *mānatva* penance as originally prescribed, and in order to remove this offense, I grant him the *karma* of absolution out of compassion."
"In this manner, he should beg for a second and a third time.
13. *Mūlāpatti-āpattivyutthāna-karman*. "In this matter, one bhikṣu should announce in the midst of the Saṃgha:
'Venerable Saṃgha, listen!'"

This bhikṣu Kālodāyin, having intentionally emitted semen, committed a saṃghāvaśeṣa offense. Without concealing this single offense, he previously requested a six-night *mānatva* from the Saṃgha, and the Saṃgha granted him the six-night *mānatva*.

While undergoing the six-night *mānatva* penance within the Saṃgha, having already practiced it for some days but not yet completed it, he commits another *saṃghāvaśeṣa* offense, which he does not conceal.

This bhikṣu Kālodāyin requested from the Saṃgha the *yadbhūyaḥkaraṇīya* (formal act of furtherance) for his original offense; the Saṃgha granted him the *yadbhūyaḥkaraṇīya*, and he completed its performance.
Now, in order to remove this offense, he requests from the Saṃgha the *āpattivyutthāpana-karman* (the formal act of emergence from guilt).
He said: "Venerable Sangha!

If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, then since the Bhikṣu Kātyāyana committed the offense of *saṃghāvaśeṣa* by intentionally emitting semen, and having not concealed this single offense, he has requested from the Saṃgha the *yathādharma* penance and completed its performance; therefore, for the purpose of removing this offense, the *āpattivyutthāna-karman* should be granted to him.
Thus it was announced.

The formal act of *jñapti-caturtha-karman* [was as follows]: "The Saṃgha grants the monk Kālodāyin, who has committed one offense of *saṃghāvaśeṣa* for intentionally emitting semen and has not concealed it, the *āpattivyutthāna-karman* (the ritual for emerging from the offense)."
“Since the Saṃgha remains silent, this matter is thus upheld.

This *karmavācanā* for the removal of offenses must be performed before twenty people; through three formal proclamations (*trivācanā*), it may be accomplished by four. Regarding the method for repentance of *sthūlātyaya*: all *sthūlātyaya* offenses arise from the two categories [of the *Prātimokṣa*], with four distinctions among them. Those of the highest grade cannot be repented of;
however, those of the lowest grade from the preceding category and those of the middle grade from the subsequent category may be repented of by four people outside the boundary (*sīmā*).
...of the remaining people of inferior grade, once they have performed the repentance: "Venerable Saṃgha, please attend to me with one mind!
I, bhikṣu [Name], having stolen four coins, have incurred a sthūlātyaya offense."
"Now, within this Sangha, a *sthūlātyaya* offense is being confessed; it is not permissible to conceal the offense.
Thus he speaks three times.
The Sangha asks:
"Do you see your own fault? He replied, "I see it."
“Do not do it again. “Venerable sir, please attend to me with one-pointed mind!
This bhikṣu, so-and-so, took hold of a woman’s body garment, thereby committing a sthūlātyaya, a grave offense.”
"I, Bhikṣu [Name], now confess my offense before the Elder; I do not conceal it.
Thus he says three times: "Elder, please attend to me with a single mind!
I, Bhikṣu [Name], having kept an extra robe for more than ten days, have committed an offense of *niḥsargika-pāyattika*."
"I, [Name], having discarded this robe, confess my offense before the Elder for the sake of purification.
Thus he says three times.
"Elder, please attend to me with one-pointed mind!"
I, bhikṣu [name], have intentionally uttered a falsehood and have incurred a pāyattika offense.
I, bhikṣu [name], now request the Venerable One to acknowledge my offense, purify me from it, and release me from it for the sake of purification.
Thus it was said three times. 15.
The Procedure for the Fourfold Confession: "Venerable Saṃgha, please attend to me with one mind!
I, the bhikṣu [Name], have fallen into a censurable matter, which is not appropriate; this is a matter that can be cleared away, and I now clear it away."
"A second and third time, speak thus; the Saṃgha replies, 'We listen.
'Venerable ones, attend with one-pointed mind!
I, the bhikṣu [Name], have touched the garment of a woman and committed a duṣkṛta offense.'"
Thus it was said three times.

Now the *karmavācanā* of extinction shall be performed, such that he shall not dwell together with us nor engage in communal affairs.

Now the Saṃgha shall perform the *nihsargika-karman* (act of exclusion) against [Name], such that he shall not dwell together with us nor engage in communal affairs.

Which Elders approve of performing the *nihsargika-karman* against the bhikṣu [Name], who has committed an act of sexual intercourse and incurred a *pārājika* offense—let those who approve remain silent;
whoever does not approve, let them speak.
The second and third times were spoken in the same manner:
"The Saṃgha has completed the formal act of *karmavācanā* for the monk so-and-so, who committed an act of sexual intercourse and incurred a *pārājika* offense."
“Since the Saṃgha remains silent, this matter is held thus. “Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
A certain bhikṣu has committed an offense, yet he does not perceive his own offense.”

If the time is ripe for the Sangha, may the Sangha grant its consent and listen: this bhikṣu so-and-so has committed an offense but does not perceive it; the Sangha shall perform the formal act of suspension for one who does not acknowledge their offense (*adarśana-pratiniḥsarga-karman*).
Thus it is announced.
The formal act of *jñapti-caturtha-karman*: "Venerable Sangha!

This bhikṣu named So-and-so has committed an offense but does not recognize it; the formal act of *adarśana-pratiniḥsarga* (expulsion for failure to acknowledge an offense) against him is now concluded."
“Since the Saṃgha remains silent, this matter is thus upheld. “Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
A certain bhikṣu has committed an offense and recognized the offense, yet he does not perform a formal confession in accordance with the Dharma.”

If the time is ripe for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha listen with patience: the monk so-and-so has committed an offense and recognized the offense, yet has not performed the proper confession; therefore, the formal act of *pravāsanīya-karman* (banishment) shall be carried out against him for his failure to do what ought to be done.
Thus it is announced.
The second motion (jñapti-dvitīya-karman): "O Saṃgha!

The bhikṣu so-and-so committed an offense and, having recognized the offense, failed to perform the Dharma-compliant confession; therefore, the formal act of suspension (pravāsanīya-karman) has been completed against him."
“Since the Saṃgha remains silent, this matter is thus upheld. 17.
Regarding the *saṃghakarma* that clarifies the ability to terminate an illegal *saṃghakarma*: A single bhikṣu should announce within the Saṃgha:
“Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
"We shall settle this matter within our own community of monks.
A monk lacking wisdom says:
"This matter should not be settled in such and such a way; this matter should be settled in such and such a way."
"I shall now perform the *karmavācanā* within the Saṃgha; the entire Saṃgha should issue a formal injunction to extinguish this matter.
Thus is the motion (*jñapti*).
[The *Tripudgala* then] proclaims the names of the four bhikṣus from the southwest and the four bhikṣus from the east within the Saṃgha.
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
These eight persons are the four bhikṣus from the southwest and the four bhikṣus from the east.
If the time is right for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha grant its consent; these eight persons are capable of adjudicating the matter and shall enter the midst of the Saṃgha to extinguish this dispute."
Thus he announces.
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
These eight persons are being proclaimed: four bhikṣus from the east and four bhikṣus from the southwest."
The Saṃgha listens: these eight persons are deciding a legal matter and have entered the midst of the Saṃgha desiring to settle this matter.

Among you here, who among the elders approves of these eight persons deciding the matter and entering the midst of the Saṃgha desiring to settle it—let him remain silent; whoever does not approve, let him speak.
“The Saṃgha has listened; these eight persons who adjudicated the matter have entered the midst of the Saṃgha and wish to terminate this matter.
Since the Saṃgha consents by remaining silent, this matter shall be upheld accordingly.”
A single bhikṣu should announce within the Saṃgha:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
This bhikṣu Ajita has been ordained for five years; though young, he is able to recite and uphold the Vinaya."

If it is the time for the Saṃgha and the Saṃgha is willing to listen, let the Saṃgha authorize the bhikṣu Ajita to act as the adjudicator of the matter and to spread out the sitting mats for the elder monks in the Bhāgīrathī Grove.
"Thus it is announced.
[The motion for] the second *karmavācanā* follows:
"May the Saṃgha listen: the bhikṣu Ajita has finished arranging his sitting mat to act as the adjudicator of the case."
"Since the Saṃgha remains silent, this matter is thus upheld.
When performing the *karmavācanā*, one follows the procedure as in the formal motion (*jñapti*), with only the following difference: "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!..."

A certain bhikṣu wishes to go beyond the boundary for the sake of a monastic matter lasting thirty-nine nights, yet he intends to enter the rains retreat within that same area and perform the *pravāraṇā* ceremony there.

If it is the proper time for the Saṃgha, may the Saṃgha grant its consent and listen: this certain bhikṣu shall go beyond the boundary for the sake of a monastic matter lasting thirty-nine nights, yet he shall enter the rains retreat within that same area and perform the *pravāraṇā* ceremony there.
Thus he makes the motion: "Venerable Saṃgha, listen!

This bhikṣu, named [Name], has gone beyond the boundary for the sake of a Saṃgha matter lasting thirty-nine nights; he shall observe the rains retreat within this very area and perform the *pravāraṇā* ceremony within this very area."

"Whichever elders consent that this bhikṣu named [Name] may go beyond the boundary for the sake of the Saṃgha's business for thirty-nine nights, yet remain within this very area for the rains retreat and perform the *pravāraṇā* ceremony within this very area—let those who consent remain silent;
whoever does not consent, let that elder speak."

“The Sangha grants this bhikṣu, so-and-so, permission for thirty-nine nights to go outside the boundary for the sake of Sangha business; he shall remain in retreat within these limits and complete the *pravāraṇā* ceremony within these limits.”
"Since the Saṃgha has consented by remaining silent, this matter is thus upheld.
18. The Rules for the Kaṭhina Robe. The Buddha was staying in Śrāvastī.
When the bhikṣus had completed their summer retreat and the *pravāraṇā* ceremony in the kingdom of Saṃkassa, they traveled together with their robes and bowls to Śrāvastī.
At that time, there was rain, muddy water, wind, and heat, and the bhikṣus were utterly exhausted.
Arriving at the Buddha’s dwelling, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet and sat to one side.
It is the constant custom of all Buddhas to inquire of the bhikṣus:
"Was your summer retreat free from want? Were you not unhappy?"
"Are you not weary from the journey? The bhikṣus replied,
"We are neither lacking nor distressed."
"You are utterly exhausted from the road.
The Buddha asked the bhikṣus, "Your affairs are all well; why are you alone so utterly exhausted?"
The bhikṣus said:

“We completed the *pravāraṇā* ceremony after our summer retreat in the kingdom of Saṃkassa; we traveled together with our robes and bowls to Śrāvastī, where we suffered greatly from the rain, muddy waters, wind, and heat.”
The Buddha said:
"From this day forward, I authorize you to remain apart from your original robes without fault once the kaṭhina robe has been formally accepted.
It should be done in this manner."
When the Saṃgha has assembled with a single mind, one bhikṣu among them should announce:
"Venerable Saṃgha, listen!
Today the Saṃgha shall make the kaṭhina robe; today the Saṃgha intends to make the kaṭhina robe."
"If the time for the Saṃgha has come, may the Saṃgha listen with patience; the Saṃgha shall now, with one mind, prepare the kaṭhina robe.
Thus is the motion.
"In due order, one should proclaim the person who shall prepare the kaṭhina robe."
One should speak thus:
"Who among the Sangha is able to act as the person who prepares the kaṭhina robe?
If there is a bhikṣu who says:
"I can do it. There are five qualities by which one should not be appointed to perform the *kaṭhina*:
being subject to desire, hatred, fear, delusion, or lacking knowledge of what has been done and what has not been done.
There are five qualities that one should be made to perform:
being without attachment, without malice, without fear, without delusion, and knowing what has been done and what has not been done.
A single bhikṣu should announce this in the midst of the Saṃgha as follows:
